messages.content: Act as a very skeptical research reviewer. Return JSON only. We seek a new, executable failure mechanism in learned predictive control under a benign-data setting: the experimenter may contribute only physically legal interaction tuples or make prediction queries; labels, rewards, observations, frames, parameters, and planner code remain untouched. The implementation must run now in official TD-MPC2 mt30-48M or upstream MBRL-Lib GaussianMLP+ModelEnv+CEM already in the repository. Previously rejected: ordinary multi-step model error, ensemble disagreement collapse, SimNorm/representation changes, parity/composition/frequency/semigroup sampling artifacts, task-family cascade, Bellman/self-label effects, corrective-data starvation, categorical reward support at native horizon 3, and CEM boundary covariance effects (matched interior control showed nearly identical contraction; return differences tracked coverage/model error). Exclude known poisoning, backdoors, reward/cost/safety manipulation, tail ranking, action execution mismatch, and generic multitask interference. Require a causal operator-level distinction, matched sham, one-step and on-policy controls, a native planner outcome gate, and a short CPU test. If nothing plausibly reaches novelty 7.0 and is directly runnable, return an empty candidate list and explain why.

{"task": "Round8 search for benign-data predictive-control failure mechanisms", "required_fields": ["candidate_id", "mechanism_cn", "carrier_and_exact_code_path", "allowed_operation", "distinction_from_rejected_families", "causal_invariant", "matched_sham", "short_test_protocol", "predicted_failure_pattern", "novelty_score", "fatal_risk"], "max_candidates": 3}
